What it shows

  • With ample chargers the search is one node. The relaxation has the integer optimum, the rounding finds it, and cancho-solve proves it at the root: 2,304 to 11,520 columns in 0.04 s to 0.77 s. HiGHS, SCIP and CBC take 0.055 s to 0.067 s on the largest, so we are 12x to 14x behind there; most of that is the LP (our sparse engine takes 0.69 s on the relaxation of the largest, HiGHS 0.044 s: 16x, and the factor grows with the size: 3x on the smallest).
  • With tight chargers we finish only the smaller sizes, and slowly. At 24x16 (768 columns) cancho-solve proves the optimum in 30.7 s and 128,510 nodes; HiGHS needs 0.86 s, SCIP 2.29 s and CBC 0.12 s. From the next size up we do not finish in 90 s.
  • The sizes of 10 seconds or more. 36x20, 48x24, 60x26: at least one of HiGHS, SCIP and CBC needs 10 s or more there (or hits the 90 s limit), and cancho-solve is at the limit on all of them. These are the sizes where the comparison is about the search and not about start-up.
  • Where the time goes. The relaxation of every tight size is solved in at most 0.047 s by every solver, ours included, and its bound is already within a fraction of a percent of the optimum; the work is in finding and proving the integer plan. Our cuts (design.md 19.8) move the root bound to the optimum at 24x16, and still the search needs 128,510 nodes to find the plan: by the evidence of this table what is missing is not a bound but a way of finding the optimal plan quickly (a stronger primal heuristic); we have not measured what the others do inside.
  • Before and after. The first run of this benchmark, on the search as it was (56a7283), needed 30,631 nodes for the ample 12x12 model (2.5 s) and did not finish the ample 48x24 in 30 s; the rounding that found no incumbent was the cause, and design.md 19.8 describes the repair. The ample column of the table is the result.
  • The dense tableau cannot hold the largest sizes. The ample 144x40 model has 11,520 columns and 11,744 rows, a tableau of 273 million cells against a ceiling of 32 million; only the sparse engine (the auto choice) solves it.

Machine: macOS-26.2-arm64-arm-64bit-Mach-O, arm64. OR-Tools 9.15.6755. Limit 90s per solve; ours is the time of solve run minus solve check (minimum of 3 runs under 5 s), the others the solver call alone with the model already built, which favours them by their own model building. Produced by python3 scripts/bench_scaling.py; the design is design.md section 21. Every optimal value agrees with HiGHS to 1e-6.
